unit.why: A short anecdote: R. Baruch of Medzhibozh weeps at the news of R. Levi Yitzhak of Berdichev's death, the messenger dies, and R. Baruch explains his lifelong opposition, followed by a moral lesson.

stories.start_quote: הרה״ק רבי ר' ברוך ממעזבוז ז"ל הי' בר פלוגתי׳
stories.end_quote: כי מי יודע מה צפון בלבו בזה
stories.summary_en: R. Baruch of Medzhibozh, a lifelong opponent of R. Levi Yitzhak of Berdichev, weeps when a follower brings news of his death; the messenger does not live out the year, and R. Baruch explains that he had disparaged Levi Yitzhak only to quiet the jealous seraphim, a lesson against speaking ill of any tzaddik.

tags.why: Lifelong dispute between R. Baruch and the Berdichever is the subject.

quotes: הי' בר פלוגתי׳ של הרה״ק מבא"ד כל ימי חייו
כי מת הגאון הק׳ מו"ה לוי יצחק מבא״ד
tags.why: Death of Levi Yitzhak and of the messenger.
The messenger's death is implied as punishment for bringing the news as good tidings.
R. Baruch weeps and cries out at the news.
His worship is likened to consuming fire.

quotes: כי מה שחלק עליו ודבר עליו רעות
tags.why: The opposition is revealed after the fact to have had a hidden protective purpose.

quotes: לבלי לדבר רע ח"ו על שום צדיק הדור
tags.why: The concluding lesson forbids speaking ill of tzaddikim.
The story is explicitly framed as a moral lesson.
The lesson teaches not to doubt one's rebbe and that his heart is hidden.

missing_concepts: the tzaddik's concealment of another tzaddik's greatness to protect him from heavenly envy
